name: ZSNeo-DC1.1 — neoantigen-pulsed dendritic-cell vaccine + temozolomide
molecular_hla_fit: IDH1/IDH2 wild-type explicitly required — the one trial here whose molecular criterion directly matches this case. MGMT not restricted. Needs sufficient tumour + blood for neoantigen identification and adequate venous access for PBMC collection.
tissue_needed: Adequate banked tumour tissue for sequencing/neoantigen identification required. Confirm what was preserved from the 1.2 cm resection.
timing_window: Enrol after surgery and after completing standard concurrent chemoradiation — a more forgiving timeline than the pre-chemoradiation vaccine trials, because the vaccine is given during adjuvant temozolomide.
reported_or_note: Early-stage platform; a sibling ZSNeo-DC1.1 trial in recurrent high-grade glioma (NCT06253234) is recruiting, but no glioblastoma survival data are published yet.
contact: Xiaomin Ma · +86 518-82342973 · xiaomin.ma@zskybio.com
unverified_or_flags: Not yet recruiting; sites not posted — likely China-only. Contact the sponsor to ask about international patients and whether tissue can be shipped.

name: RNA-LP — autologous total-tumour mRNA lipid-particle vaccine
molecular_hla_fit: Requires MGMT "low-level or unmethylated"; MGMT-methylated tumours are excluded. Newly diagnosed de novo GBM (WHO grade 4). Residual post-surgical disease <=3 cm allowed. Age >=21.
tissue_needed: Fresh / viable tumour needed to amplify tumour mRNA — archival FFPE alone is not enough. Confirm viable tissue or an RNA-grade fresh-frozen sample was banked.
timing_window: After surgery; the design integrates with standard radiation + temozolomide. Adult stratum enrolment target is small (n=28).
reported_or_note: A 2024 report described rapid, marked immune activation within days of the first dose in a small first-in-human GBM cohort; survival data immature.
contact: Marcia Hodik · 352-273-5519 · wells-BTC@ufl.edu
unverified_or_flags: MGMT-methylated tumours are excluded — confirm MGMT status before pursuing this. | Needs viable/fresh tumour tissue for RNA amplification.

name: PTPRZ1 / TERT peptide vaccine, adjuvant to chemoradiation
sponsor: Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris (PI A. Carpentier)
molecular_hla_fit: Histologically confirmed glioblastoma; IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma excluded (so IDH-wildtype fits). Phase 1 requires HLA-A2 positive and PTPRZ1 expression in the tumour. Retrospective TERT-promoter and MGMT testing on archival tissue. Steroids must be <=10 mg/day prednisone-equivalent.
tissue_needed: Standard archival tissue is sufficient for the required biomarker testing.
timing_window: Starts 28–45 days after chemoradiation completion — adjuvant window, no conflict with the Stupp protocol.
reported_or_note: TERT is the target of the UCPVax telomerase-vaccine programme, which has phase 1/2 immunogenicity and some efficacy signal in other settings; this specific PTPRZ1/TERT construct is first-in-human in GBM.
contact: Pr Antoine Carpentier · +33 1 71 20 74 66 · antoine.carpentier@aphp.fr
unverified_or_flags: Phase 1 cohort needs HLA-A2 positivity and PTPRZ1 expression — confirm both before travelling. | Shared-antigen vaccine, not built from the patient's own neoantigens.

name: Autologous dendritic cells loaded with autologous tumour homogenate
molecular_hla_fit: Histologically confirmed monofocal glioblastoma. Near-complete resection (<=5 mL residual tumour) required — matches a gross-total resection. IDH/MGMT not restricted. Steroids must be <=10 mg prednisone-equivalent.
tissue_needed: Fresh viable tumour for homogenate preparation, plus leukapheresis. Confirm fresh tissue was banked.
reported_or_note: DC + tumour-lysate/homogenate vaccines have a long phase 1/2 track record in GBM with occasional survival signals but no positive randomised trial (DCVax-L remains contested).
contact: Dr Oriana Nanni · +39 0543 739266 · oriana.nanni@irst.emr.it
unverified_or_flags: Registry primary-completion date has passed — confirm the trial is still open before contacting. | Single centre, Italy; needs fresh tumour tissue.

name: Hybrid allogeneic-DC × autologous tumour-cell fusion vaccine ± pembrolizumab
sponsor: University of São Paulo General Hospital (PI J.A.M. Barbuto)
molecular_hla_fit: Histological glioblastoma with confirmed IDH status; undergoing or completed standard of care; tumour cells must be expandable in culture. No upper age limit; performance score >50.
tissue_needed: Needs viable tumour cells that can be culture-expanded — fresh tissue from the resection. Confirm availability.
reported_or_note: The São Paulo group has prior phase 1/2 experience with DC-tumour fusion vaccines; this is the first phase 3 of the approach.
contact: Prof. José Alexandre Marzãgão Barbuto · +55 11 3091-7375 · jbarbuto@icb.usp.br
unverified_or_flags: Not yet recruiting; Brazil. | Needs a viable tumour cell culture — usually must be arranged at surgery.

name: Tamavaq™ — AI-designed personalized neoantigen + tumour-antigen peptide vaccine
molecular_hla_fit: Registry inclusion text describes recurrent malignant glioma with prior surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy, a measurable lesion (RECIST), high mutation load (>10 TMB) and >=10 neoantigens, >=3 months post-op, no prior immunotherapy — despite the study title saying "newly diagnosed".
tissue_needed: Tumour tissue for sequencing and neoantigen identification.
timing_window: Tied to a maintenance-temozolomide cycle; not a fixed post-op window.
reported_or_note: First-in-human; no efficacy data. Sponsor has limited clinical track record.
contact: Ioannis G. Grigoriadis · +30 6936 592686 · biogeneadrug@gmail.com
unverified_or_flags: Eligibility text is recurrent-disease and high-TMB oriented — contradicts the "newly diagnosed" title. Clarify directly before considering. | Single small-company site; first-in-human; broad unproven multi-adjuvant design.

name: NeoVax — personalized neoantigen peptide vaccine + radiotherapy + pembrolizumab
sponsor: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute / Massachusetts General Hospital
reported_or_note: Keskin et al., Nature 2019 (n=8): 6/8 dexamethasone-free patients generated polyfunctional neoantigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells that trafficked into the tumour; dexamethasone abrogated responses; no serious treatment-related toxicity; no survival benefit demonstrated in this tiny cohort.
unverified_or_flags: Not enrolling. This is the reference platform — the version every peptide entry in this atlas is measured against — so it is here for its data and as the group most likely to open a successor. Ask Dana-Farber neuro-oncology what is next.

name: GNOS-PV01 — personalized neoantigen DNA vaccine (± IL-12 / retifanlimab)
sponsor: Washington University School of Medicine, St Louis
reported_or_note: Nature Cancer 2026 (GT-20, n=9): up to 40 neoantigens/patient, no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities; 8/9 evaluable patients developed measurable immune responses (the non-responder received dexamethasone); reported as generating "robust immune responses and encouraging survival outcomes" — uncontrolled.
unverified_or_flags: Not enrolling, and restricted to MGMT-unmethylated disease. Included because its 2026 readout is one of the most encouraging in the field and Washington University is an active successor site to watch.

name: GAPVAC-101 — APVAC1 + APVAC2 fully personalized peptide vaccine
sponsor: DKFZ / DKTK, Heidelberg & Tübingen (led by W. Wick)
reported_or_note: Hilf et al., Nature 2019 (n=15 vaccinated): median PFS 14.2 months and median OS 29 months from diagnosis; APVAC1 drove sustained central-memory CD8 responses, APVAC2 predominantly CD4. Proof of concept for fully personalized vaccination; not powered for efficacy.
unverified_or_flags: Completed after a 16-patient feasibility cohort with no confirmatory trial to follow. The same Heidelberg group defined the RTK II methylation class this whole dashboard is built around, so this is the most directly relevant lineage — but there is nothing to enrol in. It also feeds the German private route (see CeGaT in Section 2).

name: XS15-adjuvanted multipeptide vaccination + standard chemoradiation
reported_or_note: Completed phase 1; immunogenicity read-out with XS15 as a strong T-cell adjuvant. No efficacy claim.
unverified_or_flags: Completed in 2024. Restricted to MGMT-methylated, HLA-A2-positive patients. Listed because it is the academic backbone of the Tübingen peptide-vaccine ecosystem that also runs the CeGaT private route in Section 2.

name: SurVaxM (SURVIVE)
status: Randomised phase 2b, newly diagnosed; data cut-off Jul 2026, readout pending
reported_or_note: Phase 2a: 1-yr OS 93.7%, median OS 25.9 mo; phase 2b passed interim futility
unverified_or_flags: Survivin is broadly expressed regardless of methylation subclass; the most advanced shared-antigen peptide vaccine in newly diagnosed GBM. Already covered on the main dashboard.

name: SurVaxM + temozolomide
reported_or_note: Feeds the SURVIVE phase 2b
unverified_or_flags: Same antigen/product as above, earlier cohort.

name: P30-EPS
reported_or_note: Phase 1 immunogenicity; multi-antigen to reduce escape
unverified_or_flags: A multi-peptide shared-antigen design that tries to avoid rindopepimut's single-antigen failure mode.

name: Rindopepimut (ACT IV)
reported_or_note: No overall-survival benefit; recurrences were EGFRvIII-negative (antigen escape)
unverified_or_flags: Directly cautionary for RTK II: EGFRvIII is common here, but a single-antigen EGFRvIII peptide vaccine did not work. ⚠

name: PEP-CMV
reported_or_note: Prior small studies; mixed
unverified_or_flags: Requires MGMT-unmethylated status; targets CMV antigens reported in GBM.

name: UCPVax ± pembrolizumab
reported_or_note: Recurrent-GBM phase 2 (NCT04280848) completed; CD4 "helper" telomerase epitopes
unverified_or_flags: Requires MGMT-unmethylated status. Related to the TERT arm of the open Paris trial in Section 1.

name: IDH1-R132H peptide (NOA-16)
reported_or_note: 87% immune response; favourable outcomes in IDH-mutant astrocytoma
unverified_or_flags: Not applicable — this patient is IDH-wildtype. Listed so the distinction is explicit.

reported_or_note: RNA-lipid-particle vaccine (pp65 + tumour RNA) for recurrent adult GBM; recurrent-disease arm of the UF programme

name: No verified US provider of a tumour-sequenced neoantigen vaccine sold outside a trial
format: None is a tumour-sequenced neoantigen vaccine. The Montana clinics sell catalogue research peptides — BPC-157, TB-500, sermorelin, ipamorelin, thymosin-α1 — for healing, weight loss and hormones. The integrative cancer centres offer stem-cell / immune-modulation / autologous approaches, not an exome-sequencing → neoepitope-prediction → GMP-peptide pipeline.
reported_or_note: None — there is no neoantigen-vaccine service to have GBM evidence for.
cost: No such service is sold in the US --
regulatory: In the US a personalized neoantigen vaccine is an investigational biologic: it needs an FDA IND, so it is available essentially only inside a clinical trial. Selling one as a clinic service would fall outside that framework. (503A/503B compounding covers small-molecule and simple peptide compounding, not individualized therapeutic cancer vaccines.)
contact: No provider to contact. Directory of Montana "peptide" clinics: peptidebase.io/directory/state/montana-us (wellness/anti-aging peptides, not cancer vaccines).
unverified_or_flags: The nearest real thing to "printing peptides to make neoantigens" is automated flow peptide synthesis — academic (an MIT group's "Automated Flow Synthesis of Tumor Neoantigen Peptides", 2020) and the GMP high-throughput synthesis used by trial sponsors such as Dana-Farber and CeGaT — not a US clinical service. Also checked: Moderna's mRNA-4157 / BioNTech's autogene cevumeran individualized neoantigen therapies have no glioblastoma expanded-access pathway (melanoma and other trials only). If the user has a specific Montana clinic name or URL, that entry can be researched directly.
what_is_manufactured: Nothing in this category. Montana clinics compound / resell catalogue research peptides (BPC-157, TB-500, sermorelin, ipamorelin, thymosin-α1); US integrative cancer centres offer autologous immune-cell or stem-cell products - none is a tumour-sequenced neoantigen vaccine.
starting_material: n/a - no tumour is sequenced and no patient-specific vaccine is made.
patient_story: n/a - no neoantigen-vaccine service exists to have patient accounts.

name: Immunocine Cancer Center
format: Personalized to the patient's own tumour material, but not a defined-neoantigen vaccine — it is a tumour-lysate / tumour-antigen-pulsed DC product. The company does not publish a per-patient neoepitope list.
reported_or_note: No peer-reviewed glioblastoma outcome data located; company press material and testimonials only.
cost: ≈ USD 50,000 (reported); treatment delivered in Cancún -- Not itemised publicly; secondary sources put personalized DC immunotherapy of this kind at roughly USD 50,000. Request a full written quote including the US intake fees and the Cancún treatment.
regulatory: US site provides preservation/intake services only; the cellular treatment is delivered in Mexico, outside FDA oversight.
contact: Website: immunocine.com · Arizona tumour-preservation / intake office; treatment clinic in Cancún, Mexico · enquiry form on the site.
unverified_or_flags: Whether the "tumour-specific antigens" are defined neoepitopes or whole-tumour lysate is not disclosed; no GBM survival data; treatment happens outside the US. Ask for the antigen-selection method and GBM-specific outcomes in writing.
what_is_manufactured: Autologous monocyte-derived dendritic cells exposed ex vivo to "tumour-specific antigens" and re-infused, made in a cGMP lab (per the company). Not a defined-neoepitope product - no ranked neoantigen list is published.
starting_material: The patient's own tumour tissue (preserved at the Arizona intake site) plus blood / leukapheresis for monocytes.
insurance: Not billed to US insurance; treatment is in Mexico. Superbill / receipts only; out-of-network reimbursement not guaranteed.
patient_story: Company-published written and video testimonials on immunocine.com - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified.

name: Williams Cancer Institute
format: In-situ approach — it relies on antigens released by ablating the patient's own tumour. It is not a tumour-sequenced neoantigen peptide/mRNA vaccine and involves no ex-vivo peptide manufacturing.
reported_or_note: Case reports and conference material; no randomised or GBM-specific peer-reviewed outcome data located. Brain tumours are rarely the marketed indication (mostly accessible solid tumours).
cost: Self-pay; not publicly itemised — request a quote -- Not publicly itemised; self-pay. Request an itemised quote per protocol.
regulatory: US site operates as practice-of-medicine with off-label intratumoral drug use; some protocols delivered at the Mexico site.
contact: Website: williamscancerinstitute.com · Las Vegas, Nevada (plus a Mexico site) · consultation request on the site.
unverified_or_flags: Included only to be explicit that this well-known US "personalized cancer vaccine" marketing is in-situ ablation, a different technique from the neoantigen peptide vaccine this atlas is about. No GBM efficacy data.
what_is_manufactured: No ex-vivo product. The "vaccine" is the patient's own tumour ablated in situ (pulsed electric field / cryoablation) plus intratumoral checkpoint and cytokine injections - a different technique from a peptide/mRNA neoantigen vaccine.
starting_material: The tumour in situ; no tissue is harvested for manufacturing and no sequencing-based neoepitope selection is done.
insurance: Self-pay; no insurance billing pathway described.
patient_story: Clinic-published patient videos / testimonials (williamscancerinstitute.com) - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified.

name: United States academic route (context) — NeoVax / Washington University
reported_or_note: See the landmark cards — NeoVax (Keskin, Nature 2019) and the WashU DNA vaccine (Nature Cancer 2026).
cost: Trial — no charge for the investigational product -- Trial — no charge for the investigational product.
contact: Dana-Farber neuro-oncology - dana-farber.org · Washington University / Siteman - siteman.wustl.edu · full trial records via the landmark cards at the end of this page.
unverified_or_flags: Nothing to purchase; the point of this row is that the honest US route is a trial, and there is currently a gap between trials to watch.
what_is_manufactured: NeoVax: up to ~20 GMP synthetic long peptides spanning personal neoepitopes, + poly-ICLC. Washington University: a plasmid DNA construct encoding up to ~40 neoantigens (+ an IL-12 plasmid), delivered by electroporation.
starting_material: Tumour + matched normal (blood) for whole-exome / RNA sequencing and HLA typing; requires adequate banked tumour tissue.
insurance: Trial - the investigational product is provided at no cost; standard-of-care items are billed as usual.
patient_story: No clinic testimonials; see the published trial reports (Keskin, Nature 2019; Nature Cancer 2026).

name: CeGaT GmbH / cecava GmbH
format: Fully personalized — built from the patient's own tumour mutations.
reported_or_note: 173-patient real-world series (Nature Communications 2024): median OS 31.9 months from diagnosis across all vaccinees (70 vaccinated before progression, 103 after); patients with multiple vaccine-induced T-cell responses 53 months vs 27 months for none/low (P=0.03); vaccine-induced immune response in 87/97 (90%) monitored; adverse events mostly grade 1–2.
cost: ≈ €52,000 total (€10k diagnostics + €39k vaccine + €3k monitoring) -- Reported in case accounts: ~€10,000 neoantigen diagnostics; ~€39,000 vaccine; ~€3,000 immune monitoring (one family cited ~£30,000 for the peptides). Totals vary; get an itemised quote.
regulatory: Legal in Germany as an individual named-patient treatment (individueller Heilversuch). Not an EMA marketing authorisation and not an efficacy approval. NCT05356312 is CeGaT's own expanded-access registry listing.
contact: cegat.com · cecava.com · expanded-access contact Dr Saskia Biskup (Saskia.Biskup@humangenetik-tuebingen.de)
unverified_or_flags: An independent Neuro-Oncology 2025 commentary ("Lessons ignored?") argues the survival figures are inflated by selection bias (65% of patients KPS 90–100; international travel required; median 10.4 months from diagnosis to vaccination → lead-time bias; median follow-up only 21.3 months), uncontrolled external comparators, non-prespecified immune-response criteria, incomplete adverse-event reporting, and that 19 of 50 authors are affiliated with the provider. The number of patients sequenced but never vaccinated is not reported. No randomised data.
what_is_manufactured: GMP synthetic peptides spanning the patient's predicted neoepitopes, formulated with adjuvant - the "printing" step done with identity/purity/sterility release testing. ~12 weeks from diagnostics.
starting_material: Tumour tissue (FFPE or fresh) + blood, for tumour-exome sequencing, HLA typing and neoantigen prediction (CancerNeo®).
insurance: German statutory insurance rarely covers it; private German insurers sometimes reimburse partially, case by case. Not billed to non-German (e.g. US) insurance.
patient_story: Named-patient accounts appear in UK press and fundraising coverage (e.g. Brain Tumour Research features); the provider does not host a testimonial page. Outcomes in those accounts are not independently verified.

name: Hallwang Private Oncology Clinic
format: Claimed personalized; methodology not independently documented.
reported_or_note: No peer-reviewed glioblastoma outcome data; the clinic does not publish survival data.
cost: ≈ USD 100,000–127,000 per 1–3-week programme; ~80% deposit upfront -- Documented cases ~USD 100,000–127,000 for a 1–3-week programme; ~80% deposit required upfront.
regulatory: German individual healing attempt. No insurance contracts of any kind (clinic states this explicitly).
contact: hallwang-clinic.com · +49 7443 9642 40
unverified_or_flags: Independent reporting (Science-Based Medicine and others) has specifically named this clinic for selling unproven, ineffective therapies alongside legitimate-sounding ones; GoFundMe banned Hallwang fundraisers in 2019. Also catalogued on the main dashboard's private-provider list. Scrutinise closely.
what_is_manufactured: Not disclosed for the peptide component. Broad personalised-oncology menu also includes dendritic-cell, NK and T-cell products and off-label drug combinations; the peptide-vaccine methodology is not published.
starting_material: Blood and/or tumour material, varies by protocol (not independently confirmed).
insurance: Clinic states plainly it has no contracts with any statutory or private health insurer; costs are settled directly by the patient, with ~80% due upfront. No billing pathway offered.
patient_story: Clinic-published testimonials (hallwang-clinic.com/en/experiences) - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified. GoFundMe banned Hallwang fundraisers in 2019.

name: IOZK (Institut für Onkologische Immunologie)
format: Personalized (autologous tumour lysate + own dendritic cells).
reported_or_note: Single-institution case series in IDH-wildtype GBM reporting improved OS vs historical published data (PMC 2023); not randomised.
cost: ≈ €65,000 for the first two cycles + mandatory diagnostics -- ~€23,000–26,000 per vaccination cycle; ~€65,000 for the first two cycles plus mandatory diagnostics.
regulatory: German individual healing attempt / hospital exemption.
unverified_or_flags: Covered in full on the main dashboard. Included here only to be clear it is a DC vaccine, not the peptide/neoantigen modality this atlas is about.
what_is_manufactured: IO-Vac® autologous dendritic-cell vaccine matured with oncolytic Newcastle disease virus - a cell product, not a peptide/neoantigen vaccine. Optional 5-day immunogenic-cell-death add-on.
starting_material: Tumour tissue (autologous lysate) + blood (for monocyte-derived dendritic cells).
insurance: German statutory insurance rarely covers it without dispute; private German insurers sometimes reimburse partially. Not billed to non-German insurance.
patient_story: None currently listed by the institute.

name: NEO CLINIC TOKYO
format: Claimed personalized — NGS-based mutation calling. Number of peptides, prediction method and manufacturer not published on the English site.
reported_or_note: None published. No patient numbers, no GBM-specific data, no outcome data of any kind on the public site.
cost: Not published — self-pay; request a full itemised quote -- Not published — request a full itemised quote. Japanese neoantigen/DC peptide services are typically fully out of pocket and not covered by Japanese or foreign insurance.
regulatory: Japan free-market medicine (jiyū shinryō) under the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine — a safety notification framework, not an efficacy review.
contact: neoclinic-en.jp · +81 3-6450-4796
unverified_or_flags: Essentially everything about effectiveness. No methodology, no denominator, no GBM experience is disclosed. Treat as unverified and ask for the sequencing report, neoepitope list, peptide Certificates of Analysis and any GBM outcomes in writing.
what_is_manufactured: A neoantigen peptide vaccine and, separately, a shared "oncoantigen" peptide vaccine. Peptide count, prediction pipeline and the synthesis contractor are not disclosed on the public site.
starting_material: Tumour tissue for NGS-based mutation calling + blood; specifics (fresh vs archival, tumour-content threshold) not published.
insurance: Fully out of pocket; not covered by Japan's National Health Insurance or by foreign / international insurance.

name: Personalized Peptide Vaccination (PPV) — Kurume University lineage / Brightpath Biotherapeutics
format: Per-patient selection from a shared pool — not built from the patient's own mutations. A fully personalized neoantigen successor is in development.
reported_or_note: Two decades of Japanese phase 1/2 work across many cancers, including limited glioma. Multiple randomised phase 2/3 trials in other tumours (e.g. castration-resistant prostate, biliary tract) were negative for overall survival. No positive randomised GBM data.
cost: ≈ ¥44,000–66,000 per antigen; full-course price not itemised -- Historically ~¥44,000–66,000 per antigen in the advanced-medical-care setting; total course cost not publicly itemised.
regulatory: Advanced Medical Care / research framework in Japan; not funded by national insurance for general use.
contact: Brightpath Biotherapeutics, Tokyo - brightpathbio.com · Kurume University Hospital cancer-vaccine outpatient clinic.
unverified_or_flags: The classic PPV method has largely failed its controlled trials elsewhere; applicability to newly-diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM is unproven. The neoantigen successor has no GBM data yet.
what_is_manufactured: Classic PPV: 2-4 pre-manufactured shared-antigen peptides selected per patient from a fixed ~30-peptide pool, given with an adjuvant. Brightpath's fully personalized neoantigen successor is still in development.
starting_material: Blood only in classic PPV - HLA-A typing plus measurement of pre-existing peptide-specific IgG to pick the 2-4 peptides. No tumour sequencing.
insurance: Advanced Medical Care / research setting; not funded by Japan's national insurance for general use; not covered by foreign insurance.

contact: immunitytherapycenter.com · hope4cancer.com · chipsahospital.org · issels.com - Issels and Hope4Cancer are also on the main dashboard.
unverified_or_flags: Any "neoantigen vaccine" marketing from a Mexican integrative clinic should be treated as unverified until they provide the sequencing report, the ranked neoepitope list, peptide Certificates of Analysis, GMP documentation, and GBM-specific (not all-comers) outcomes in writing. None of that was found in public materials.
what_is_manufactured: Marketed "cancer vaccines", dendritic-cell products, and autologous "autohemotherapy" inside broad 3-week integrative programmes. No exome → neoepitope → GMP-peptide pipeline is documented at any of them.
starting_material: Blood and/or tumour material, varies by clinic; not independently confirmed. No published sequencing-based neoantigen workflow.
insurance: Cannot bill US insurance (treatment in Mexico); some PPO out-of-country plans reimburse partially if pre-verified; the clinics disclaim any guarantee.
patient_story: Clinic-published patient journeys (e.g. Hope4Cancer's "Aaron - stage IV glioblastoma" story) - not independently verified; weigh a single account against the absence of peer-reviewed data.
